extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for geometry problem solving, consisting of 3,002 high-school geometry problems with dense annotations in formal language. The dataset includes problem text, geometry diagrams, multiple-choice candidate answers, and correct answers. Each problem is annotated with formal language descriptions to bridge the semantic gap between textual and visual contents, enabling symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.publisher: Center for Vision, Cognition, Learning and Autonomy, UCLA; College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University; School of Intelligent Systems Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University; Beijing Institute of General Artificial Intelligence; Peking University; Tsinghua University
extraction.citeAs: Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Geometry3K dataset was collected from two popular high-school textbooks across grades 6-12 via online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. The dataset was annotated with dense formal language descriptions to enable symbolic reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry3K was collected from high-school textbooks (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline) and includes problem text, geometry diagrams, multiple-choice candidate answers, and correct answers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was preprocessed to include formal language annotations for both problem text and diagrams. The text parser used rule-based methods with regular expressions, while the diagram parser used Hough Transformation for primitive extraction, RetinaNet for symbol detection, and MathPix for OCR. The formal language annotations bridge the semantic gap between textual and visual contents.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem in Geometry3K is annotated with dense formal language descriptions that include predicates and literals for geometric shapes, attributes, relations, and numerical values. The annotations are used to train and evaluate problem parsers and symbolic solvers. The formal language is defined with 91 predicates categorized into geometric shapes, unary attributes, general attributes, binary relations, A-IsXOf-B-type relations, and numerical attributes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process involved manual collection by trained annotators and formal language descriptions to enable symbolic reasoning. The formal language annotations are used to train problem parsers and symbolic solvers, ensuring consistency and interpretability in the dataset.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were well-trained with undergraduate degrees and had high-school or higher education backgrounds. The dataset also includes human performance evaluations from crowdsourcing (Amazon Mechanical Turk) and expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RetinaNet (for diagram symbol detection), MathPix (for OCR), Hough Transformation (for primitive extraction), and rule-based text parsing with regular expressions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation baselines are released to promote follow-up work in the geometry domain. The project includes code and data availability at https://lupantech.github.io/inter-gps.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models, facilitating education in geometry problem solving. The dataset is collected from open sources and does not involve sensitive personal information.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected from high-school textbooks, which may introduce biases related to educational content and problem types. The dataset includes diverse geometric shapes and problem goals but may not cover all possible variations in geometry education.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to high-school geometry problems and may not generalize to other domains. Some problems may require complex theorems or combined shapes that the current symbolic solver cannot handle. Diagram parsing may fail for ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for geometry problem-solving models. The dataset is designed for symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving, with formal language annotations to bridge the gap between textual and visual contents.
